description: Family to kernel-band routing data for the GPU backend. This file is the normative in-repo source: the runtime and tools/generate_class_tables.py read it, the runtime never carries a second copy of any mapping expressed here (registry contract section 3.3), and its content digest is reported in the certified-source binding set so a drifted copy is visible to verification.

cl100k_v3.note: Character classes P/L/N/S over the whole codepoint space, probed from the reference engine.

cl100k_m2l_v3.note: The cl100k table with Mark codepoints folded into the letter class.

deepseek_v1.note: Seven-class table for the three-splitter ruleset; carries a metadata sidecar cross-checked against the kernel inline constants.

o200k_v4.note: Seven-class table for the o200k splitter group.

kimi_v1.note: Ten-class table; letter classes exclude Han, with three Han subclasses added.

nfc_qc_v1.note: NFC quick-check table probed from the reference engine's own normalizer. Used by every family whose artifact declares an NFC normalizer; not family specific.

cl100k.note: GPT-style seven-alternative splitter plus byte-level BPE.

o200k.note: o200k splitter group; the fused entry is CUDA-Graph capturable, and the batched channel needs windowed piece starts.

kimi.note: Split-layer kernel only. There is no end-to-end encoder for this band, so end-to-end requests fall back to the reference backend.

olmo_3_7b.note: Same regex as llama_3_1_8b; the artifact's Split behaviour differs but is equivalent for a fully covering pattern.

qwen3_5_08b.note: qwen3 skeleton with Mark codepoints folded into the letter class.

ling_3_0_flash.note: Splitter is a tiktoken-style rewrite of the qwen3 pattern; the four spelling differences were shown branch-by-branch equivalent, so it maps onto the qwen3 path with no kernel change.

laguna_s_2_1.note: Stage 1 is byte-identical to qwen3_8b; stage 0 adds newline-run cut points, handled by the laguna ruleset branch in the kernel.

deepseek_v3.note: digits_max is null because it is read from the class-table metadata, which extracts it mechanically from the artifact's own pattern; keeping a copy here would be a second source of truth. The model section (vocabulary and merges) is identical to the family named by shares_model_with, so one exported table serves both; the two model sections are hashed and compared before every use, and a difference refuses the shared table.

hy3.note: Byte alphabet is not fully covered and the artifact has no unknown token; the kernel reproduces the reference behaviour of dropping unmapped initial symbols before merging.

kimi_k3.note: Split layer only: this band has no end-to-end encoder, so encode requests run on the reference backend. digits_max is 3 because the artifact's digit alternative is {1,3}; the kernel compiles that bound in, so no other value can be honoured.
